# DESIGN-ONLY EXPERIMENT SPEC — "How does the period setting P affect PDF performance on ETTm1?"
Status: specification only. **No experiment was run. No performance values are reported, predicted, or implied anywhere in this document.** Nothing in /workspace could confirm the PDF codebase or ETTm1 (evidence §E1–E6), so every model/data-specific constant is either a runner-verified placeholder or a declared adopted convention.

---
## 1. Primary arm definition (adopted convention, NOT a confirmed property of PDF)
Named config field: `period.length_steps` (alias `P`).
**Primary definition:** `P` = period length **in time steps** feeding the periodicity-aware pathway — the cycle length used for periodic decomposition / period-aligned patching / cyclic positional structure. It is **swept externally as a fixed hyperparameter** (never learned, never annealed), so "period setting" is a genuinely manipulated variable.

Status statement (binding): this is an **adopted convention under an unspecified-source constraint**. Neither the PDF architecture nor the location/units of its period mechanism is resolvable from any local source. Any statement of the form "PDF uses P as …" is out of scope here.

**Variant registry (documented alternatives, own grids, own interpretation notes; answers NOT transferable across variants):**
| Variant | Unit of swept knob | Meaningful values | Calendar mapping | Interpretation notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **primary** | steps | 1, 6, 12, 24, 48, 96, 120, 144, 168, 192, 240, 288, 576, 1008 | 6=1h, 12=2h, 24=4h, 48=8h, 96=16h, 144=1 day, 288=2 days, 1008=1 week | "best P" = best assumed cycle length |
| **(i) patch/segment granularity derived from P** | patch length in steps | 1,2,3,6,8,12,16,24,32,48,72,96,144,288 (must divide look-back; use look-back 288 for integer division of 144/288) | 6→hourly patches; 48→8 patches/day; 144→1 patch=1 day; 288→1 patch=2 days | conflates cycle hypothesis with token granularity; 1008 not representable (weekly > 2×look-back); 120/168/240 need a declared padding policy |
| **(ii) number of periods retained k, context = k×P** | cycle count k ∈ {1,2,3,4} | constraint k·P ≤ look-back; at L=96: k_max=8 (P=12), 4 (P=24), **0 (P=144)** | k = floor(L/P) | at L=96 the daily cycle is *inexpressible* (96<144): such a sweep is largely a context-depth sweep; needs look-back ≥144 to be interpretable |
| **(iii) frequency/harmonic index** | FFT bin h | h ∈ {1,2,3,4,6,8,12,24,48} on window 576 | steps = 576/h; **h=4 ↔ 144 steps (daily)** | window-dependent; weekly (1008) not representable at window 576, excluded rather than silently truncated |
Consequence stated up front: the same physical setting maps to *different* numbers per variant (daily = 144 steps = patch 144 = k depends on L = h 4), so any "best period" claim must name its variant.

## 2. Period grid and rationale (primary arm)
Anchors, not an arbitrary list. ETTm1 is 10-min sampled ⇒ **144 steps/day, 1008 steps/week** (runner-verified constant C3, §8).
- sub-daily harmonics of the day: **6, 12, 24, 48, 96** (1h, 2h, 4h, 8h, 16h)
- **144 = daily anchor** = pre-registered reference anchor
- supra-daily: **192, 288 (2 d), 576 (4 d), 1008 (1 week)**
- **off-cycle controls 120, 168, 240** — near-daily but *not* equal to the calendar day; this is what separates a periodicity explanation from a capacity/context explanation
- **P = 1** — neutralization arm (cycle collapsed; periodic pathway carries no cyclic structure)
- **detected-P** — dominant period estimated by FFT/ACF **on the train split only** (with L=96 windowing, which caps detectable periods near 48 — declared, not hidden)
Log-spaced over [1, 1008]; every value has a stated calendar interpretation, so any optimum is describable in physical units rather than as a grid index.

## 3. Arms (what is manipulated vs held fixed)
| Arm | Manipulated | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| **A1 primary (coupled)** | P only; **reference coupling preserved** — derived patch length/context follow P as the reference implementation would | headline MSE(P)/MAE(P) curve |
| **A2 capacity/context-matched** | P only, **token count frozen** (pad/trim to fixed token count) and **parameter count matched** to the P=144 model (adjust width, not P) | separates "correct cycle" from "more tokens / more parameters" |
| **A3 period-free ablation** | periodic mechanism removed (concrete edit §5); P inert by construction | licenses attribution to the *mechanism* |
| **A4 seasonal-naive** | none; deterministic forecast = value 144 steps back | scale-free floor; shows whether the daily cycle is exploited at all |
| **A5 linear anchor** | none; DLinear, L=96, no periodic pathway | sanity that A1–A3 sit in a plausible error range |
| **P1 look-back × P probe** | L ∈ {96,336} × Tier-B period subset | **secondary probe**, not a first-class factor (ruling Q6) |
| **P2 patch-length × P probe** | patch ∈ {6,12,24} × P ∈ {48,96,144}, variant (i), look-back 288 | **explicitly exploratory / hypothesis-generating only** |
Held identical across every arm and P: data split and borders; train-fitted scaler; L; H; depth/width/dropout/activation/normalization; optimizer, LR, schedule, warmup, clipping; batch size; epochs and early-stopping patience (same monitored val quantity); loss; the **same 5 seeds reused for every P (paired, never re-randomised)**; dtype, thread count, library versions (lockfile); any input permutation.
**Mandatory tabulation (all arms):** per P → `n_params`, `n_tokens_per_sample`, `pad_or_trim_amount`, `context_steps`, wall-clock, `confounded: yes/no`. Per ruling Q3, **if capacity matching is impossible at some P, that P is reported `confounded` and kept in the table — never dropped silently.** A1 and A2 curves are reported **side by side** as the primary figure.

## 4. ETTm1 evaluation protocol (adopted conventions, flagged as conventions)
- Multivariate 7-feature input, **target = OT**, output = OT. Row count/units read from the supplied file header (constants C1–C4, §8).
- Split: **temporal, no shuffling, 6:2:2** train/val/test. If the supplied code defines its own borders, the runner honours and records them; both conventions are tabulated in §E7 because they give materially different test-window counts.
- Preprocessing: standardization **fit on train only**; no test-fitted statistic anywhere; no test-time augmentation; no scaling by global (train+test) statistics.
- Sliding windows, **stride 1**; test windows start at (train+val boundary − L) so the first test window is legal; n_test(H) = n_test + L − H − 1.
- **Horizons {96, 192, 336, 720}** with **L=96** primary; **L=336** secondary probe only.
- Model selection: **validation only** (checkpoint, patience, any early stop). Test read **exactly once** per (arm, P, H, seed) after all configuration is frozen.
- Metrics: **MSE and MAE on the standardized scale (primary for statistics, scale-comparable across horizons) and on the inverse-transformed original scale (for reporting).** Both scales reported so a normalization artifact cannot masquerade as a period effect.

## 5. A3 period-free ablation — concrete architectural edit (the only attribution-licensing arm)
Because the exact PDF block is unknown, the edit is a **shape-preserving substitution plus determinism audit**, applied to whatever the block turns out to be:
1. **Locate the block** whose computation depends on `period.length_steps`: a cycle-aligned reshape `(B,L) → (B,n_cycles,P)`, a period-k moving average / seasonal index, a period-aligned patch embedding, or a cyclic-offset positional/attention bias table.
2. **Substitute a capacity-matched identity-mixing block** with the **same input/output tensor shapes and same parameter count**: replace P-dependent pooling/alignment with a plain learnable linear map over the same flattened window (equivalently: hard-fix the alignment index to `P := 1`, then restore parameter count by widening that block's projection so `n_params` matches the A1 model at P=144 within 0.5%). Trunk, loss and head byte-identical to A1.
3. **Invariance audit (hard gate, before any training):** eval mode, one fixed batch, P ∈ {48, 144, 1008}. Outputs must be **bitwise identical** across all three. Non-identical ⇒ P still enters the computation ⇒ A3 invalid; fix and re-audit.
4. **Sensitivity audit (companion hard gate, on A1):** with weights fixed, changing P **must** change the output; if it does not, P is inert in that codebase and the question is unanswerable as posed — reported as a blocker, not as a null result.

## 6. Pre-registered analysis plan (fixed before any results exist)
- Observation unit: one test-set metric per (arm, P, H, seed).
- **Statistic:** paired per-seed difference vs the daily anchor, `d_s = metric(P,H,s) − metric(144,H,s)`, same seed on both sides (seed noise cancels by pairing). Report mean `d`, paired SE, 95% paired-t interval (**df=4, t_crit=2.776** at 5 seeds).
- **Threshold rule:** P declared different from anchor iff the 95% paired-t interval excludes 0 **and** |mean d| exceeds a pre-fixed minimum effect size of 0.5 × the seed-level SE of the anchor itself — a variance-relative, not outcome-relative, threshold; deliberately **no numeric MSE target**.
- **Multiplicity:** Holm correction within each family = {arm} × {horizon} × {metric}; family size = 13 non-anchor P values (Tier A), 6 (Tier B). No pooling across arms/horizons/scales after seeing results.
- **Shape analysis (pre-registered as descriptive):** MSE vs log P with a quadratic and a 3-point moving average; report argmin location and whether it falls in the calendar-anchored neighbourhood {120,144,168} or in the off-cycle set {120,168,240} — the two sets overlap by construction, so the A1-vs-A2 contrast, not the argmin, carries the inference.
- **A3 contrast (attribution step):** A1(P) − A3 per horizon. Period sensitivity that **persists in A3** is *not* attributable to the periodicity mechanism.
- **A2 contrast:** an A1 optimum that vanishes under capacity/context matching is read as capacity/context, not periodicity.
- **Variance diagnostics:** seed SD by horizon (expect growth at 336/720); no imputation, no seed exclusion; failed runs logged with reason and counted, never silently removed.

## 7. Tiered run-count budget (sizing only — no hardware, no wall-clock assumed)
**Tier A (full), 740 runs:** A1 300 (15 P × 4 H × 5 seeds) · A2 300 · A3 20 · A4 4 · A5 20 · P1 probe 42 · P2 probe 54.
**Tier B (fallback), 92 runs:** A1 42 · A2 42 · A3 6 · A4 2, with P ⊂ {1,48,144,288,1008} ∪ {120,168}, H ∈ {96,192}, 3 seeds.
**Trigger:** Tier B only under an explicit compute limit that forbids Tier A; the choice is recorded **before** results are examined.
**What Tier B forfeits (explicit):** 5→3 seeds removes ~55% of the paired-difference precision and drops df 4→2 (t_crit 4.303), so only large effects clear the threshold; two horizons forfeit the horizon-dependence test (does the optimum move with H) and the P×H reading entirely; the 7-point grid forfeits curve shape (a quadratic/argmin fit is not defensible on it), cannot separate a shallow daily optimum from a broad 96–288 plateau, and cannot resolve sub-daily harmonics (6/12/24/48) from one another; A4/A5 anchors shrink too. Tier B supports "is any period effect detectable at the daily cycle" — **not** "where is the optimum".

## 8. Constants a runner must verify or substitute (nothing here asserted as fact)
C1 dataset row count & sampling interval (from the supplied CSV header). C2 split borders actually used (repo config vs 6:2:2 — record which, with resulting n_train/n_val/n_test). C3 steps per day (derive from C1; 144 assumed from 10-min sampling). C4 scaler fit range (train-only) and whether target and covariates are standardized jointly or separately. C5 the code path that actually reads `period.length_steps` (file:line) — filled in by the runner, then used to classify which §1 variant the repo's mechanism corresponds to. C6 the reference coupling derived from C5 (patch/context as a function of P) with `n_params`/`n_tokens` per P. C7 library/hardware lockfile. C8 seed list and RNG seeding points. Every entry C1–C8 must appear in the run manifest; unresolved entries are reported as unresolved.

## 9. Feasibility, artifacts, checklist (sizing-and-runnable only)
Feasibility: executable by an **external** runner given (a) the PDF code and (b) the ETTm1 CSV. **Not** executable in this environment — no repo, no data, no numerics stack, no network (§E1–E6). No hardware or runtime is assumed or claimed.
Runner artifacts: `config_matrix.json` (§E10) → `runs.csv` (arm, variant, P, H, L, seed, n_params, n_tokens, confounded, status) → `params_tokens_table.csv` → `test_metrics.csv` (per-seed, both scales) → `paired_diff_stats.csv` (d, SE, CI, Holm-adjusted p, threshold verdict) → `figure_A1_vs_A2_by_horizon` → `figure_lookback_probe` → `manifest.md` with C1–C8.
Pre-flight gates (must pass before training): 1 dataset sha/header verified; 2 scaler confirmed train-only; 3 no split-boundary leakage (no normalization statistic from test rows; no train target inside a test window); 4 **A3 bitwise P-invariance audit passes**; 5 **A1 P-sensitivity audit passes**; 6 `n_params`/`n_tokens` table complete or rows flagged `confounded`; 7 seeds paired identically across arms; 8 test set unopened until freeze; 9 Tier recorded; 10 analysis-plan hash recorded.

## 10. Claim boundary
Can establish: *how test error varies with the externally set period knob P for this PDF implementation on ETTm1 under the stated conventions*, and whether that variation survives capacity/context matching and survives removal of the periodic mechanism.
Cannot establish: it does **not** determine the true period of ETTm1 (P is an input, not an estimate; the detected-P arm is a reference line, not ground truth); it does not generalize across variants (i)/(ii)/(iii), across codebases, datasets, unswept horizons, or other targets. The off-cycle arms exist precisely so a capacity/context explanation can be separated from a periodicity explanation; if A2 flattens the A1 curve the licensed conclusion is "no periodicity effect detectable under these conventions", which is a valid outcome, not a failed experiment. **No ordering of P values is asserted or predicted anywhere in this document.**

## 11. Risk / limitation table
| Risk | Why it bites here | Mitigating control |
|---|---|---|
| **Unresolved PDF semantics / wrong variant mapping** | no local source pins the mechanism (Q1/Q2) | mechanism-explicit primary arm + variant registry with per-variant grids; code-path field C5; non-transferability stated in the claim boundary |
| **Capacity / token-count confound** | if patch/context derive from P, params and tokens co-vary with P (Q3) | A2 matched arm side by side; mandatory `n_params`/`n_tokens` table; unmatched P flagged `confounded`, never dropped |
| **Split-boundary & normalization convention drift** | two defensible ETTm1 conventions give very different test-window counts (§E7); a test-fitted scaler would inflate apparent sensitivity | runner records the convention (C2/C4); train-only scaler verified; leakage gate 3; both metric scales reported |
| **Horizon-dependence of the optimum** | the argmin may move with H; a single-horizon reading would misattribute | all 4 horizons in Tier A; statistics per (H, metric) family; horizon-dependence named as a pre-registered outcome |
| **Seed variance at long horizons** | fewer windows and heavier tails at 336/720 inflate variance | 5 paired seeds; paired-difference design; SD-by-horizon diagnostics; variance-relative threshold; no seed exclusion |
| **P=1008 under-supported by the test span** | only a handful of full weekly cycles in ~4 months of test data | flagged low-support in the table; interpreted descriptively only |
| **Grid non-representability / padding artifacts** | 120/168/240 don't divide L; variants (i)/(iii) can't express 1008 | padding policy declared in config; non-representable values excluded **explicitly with a reason**, never silently |
| **Multiplicity / researcher degrees of freedom** | 13 P × 4 H × 2 scales × 2 metrics invites post-hoc selection | Holm within pre-declared families; analysis-plan hash before the test pass; single test pass |
| **Mechanism sensitivity absent altogether** | P might be inert or unused in the shipped code | gate 5 turns this from a silent null into a reported blocker |
